sonnet.problem: The joke makes Jesus' promise about asking the Father in His name the punchline. It says the oven 'has given me NOTHING' right after His 'He will give you.' That sets a comparison against what Jesus says and suggests asking gets nothing.
sonnet.rule: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper. ... Comparisons stay on the human side of the moment.

sonnet.problem: No card has told the baker the Father is with Jesus (16:32). Card 8's right answer already says the disciples 'leave Him all alone,' so a thoughtful baker would reasonably pick True here. The right answer (False) can only be reached by luck.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. ... The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

sonnet.problem: The joke says the biggest move Papa Dorin ever made was across one kitchen into the junk drawer. In his backstory, the angel moving him from the drawer to the Dorinverse is a bigger move. The joke contradicts the backstory.
sonnet.rule: His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery, the junk drawer and the Millers' kitchen. They fit the backstory, never change it, and don't contradict each other in one lesson.
